correctness.rationale: The entry identity (1+a)^|A cap B| = sum_{C subset A cap B} a^|C| with a=omega-1 gives F=Z D Z^T on the downward-closed Boolean support poset; unitriangular Z proves invertibility for m>=2 and produces the exact Möbius inverse indexed by A union B. F-J differs only on pairs with intersection: at most n b_(n,r)^2 such pairs and each error <=2, giving O_r(n^(r-1/2)) Frobenius error independent of m. F^-1 differs from its origin rank-one component by union-size >=1 entries, with squared Frobenius remainder O_r(|a|^(-2r)n^(2r-1)); the dominant entry is a^-r(n^r/r!+O_r(n^(r-1))) uniformly because |a|<=2. Multiplying yields the sharp uniformly relative n^-1/2 law; rank-one gap estimates yield extremal vector claims. Independently built F, Z D Z^T and explicit inverse, checked both products for (n,r,m)=(7,1,3),(8,1,13),(7,2,5),(9,2,31), with max residual below 10^-9. Exact asymptotic needs fixed r; finite cases are not its proof.
residual_risks: The r=0 edge is only background; growing r and finite-dimensional optimal constants are not claimed.
Uniform m error follows specifically from |omega-1|<=2 and factoring |a|^-r, not from numerical observations.

value.rationale: This is a sharp reconstruction-stability law for a natural polynomial-size subset of the multivariate Fourier matrix, explaining the combined n^(2r) dimension amplification and angular blowup [2 sin(pi/m)]^-r with no relation required between n and m. The extremal singular-vector localization identifies which coordinates cause instability. A growing modulus changes the actual numerical difficulty; this is not merely applying fixed-q conditioning with a renamed parameter.
residual_risks: No estimates for growing support radius r or exact finite spectrum; the condition number can be much larger at finite n than asymptotic leading term.

final_claim: For fixed integer radius r>=1, arbitrary integers m>=3 (even varying arbitrarily with n), and Boolean-word support ball of subsets |A|<=r in (Z/mZ)^n, the unnormalized principal Fourier matrix F(A,B)=omega^|A cap B| has spectral norms n^r/r!(1+O_r(n^-1/2)) and n^r/(r! |omega-1|^r)(1+O_r(n^-1/2)) for its inverse, and sharp condition n^(2r)/((r!)^2 [2 sin(pi/m)]^r)(1+O_r(n^-1/2)); singular vectors localize at the constant and empty-set directions.
